      <title>US grants deportation reprieve to migrants from Ukraine and Sudan</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/19/us-migrants-deportation-ukraine-sudan</link>
      <description><p>DHS says migrants ‘retain protections’ after temporary protected status was set to expire on Monday</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/15/immigration-trump-midterms-reader-q-a">Send us your questions about immigration and the midterms</a></p></li></ul><p>More than 100,000 people from Ukraine and Sudan can stay in the United States without immediate risk of deportation, the Department of Homeland Security said, in what amounts to a temporary reprieve after their right to stay in the country was set to expire on Monday.</p><p>Temporary protected status was set to end on Monday for about 101,000 Ukrainians and 1,800 Sudanese. But the DHS said an announcement “will be made at the appropriate time”. Until then, the department said in a written statement, Ukrainians and Sudanese in the US covered by those temporary measures “retain protection”. The department did not indicate how long they could stay or when a final announcement would be made on their status.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/19/us-migrants-deportation-ukraine-sudan">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/kenya-starvation-cult-leader-guilty-murder-190-children</link>
      <description><p>Paul Mackenzie and his church set up sect that ordered followers to starve themselves and their children, say prosecutors</p><p>A Kenyan court has found the starvation cult leader Paul Mackenzie and about 30 others guilty of murder over the deaths of ⁠190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult-related disasters in recent history.</p><p>Mackenzie was arrested in 2023 after police received a tipoff, and weeks later authorities began uncovering bodies in shallow graves in the Shakahola forest near the coast ⁠in south-eastern Kenya.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/kenya-starvation-cult-leader-guilty-murder-190-children">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/drone-attack-market-al-dibab-west-kordofan-sudan</link>
      <description><p>Witness says drone struck twice at transport hub in al-Dibab, in one of deadliest single attacks of war</p><p>A drone strike near a market in southern Sudan on Sunday evening killed 80 people, mostly commuters catching rides home.</p><p>Ahmed Wadi, a witness, said the attack in the town of al-Dibab in West Kordofan state left “50 bodies who I helped bury, one of them my own brother Mohamed”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/drone-attack-market-al-dibab-west-kordofan-sudan">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Ebola cases in Kenya highlight US failures amid Trump cuts to key services</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/ebola-cases-kenya-us-quarantine</link>
      <description><p>Opposition to US-led quarantine center in Kenya follows sweeping funding cuts and withdrawal from WHO</p><p>An eighth person in Kenya has tested positive for the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola in the country’s first-ever cluster of cases of the virus, as the second-largest outbreak in history has killed more than 4,300 and sickened more than 9,000 people in the region.</p><p>It highlights the diminished role the US has played in the worsening Ebola outbreak by building a controversial quarantine center in Kenya, pulling back health support globally, and banning travelers from certain countries. All of this has also reduced the ability to identify and respond to the outbreak and exacerbated mistrust.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/ebola-cases-kenya-us-quarantine">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Hilarious quips and ‘100,000-volt’ energy: the hypemen (and women) redefining Afrobeats music</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/18/lagos-hypemen-redefining-afrobeats-music-afrohype</link>
      <description><p>Style of emceeing based on high-octane, ad-libbed vocals has flourished thanks to its unique way of captivating crowds</p><p>For the 2015 freshmen cohort of the history degree programme at the University of Lagos, their classmate’s first-semester presentation was so captivating that they began calling him Toby Shang, after the 16th-century Chinese dynasty he had focused on.</p><p>His crowd engagement that day had been harnessed from his high school days as a ginger-man (energiser) in a three-man band and as a private tutor. By his final year at university, his viral catchphrases and infectious energy had resulted in a hit song, Shedibalabala. Today, he is one of the self-acclaimed “evangelists and pioneers” in the Afrobeats sub-genre some are now calling Afrohype or lamba.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/18/lagos-hypemen-redefining-afrobeats-music-afrohype">Continue reading...</a></description>

News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 18:09:49 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>France</category><title>How French police are harnessing social media to identify looters</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261020-how-french-police-are-harnessing-social-media-to-identify-looters</link><description>
French police are turning to social media to identify and arrest suspects linked to last weekend’s looting and unrest. Investigators are scrutinising videos posted online alongside footage from thousands of security cameras to track suspects and gather evidence. The crackdown comes as the government vows to hold those responsible for the violence and damage to shops accountable.
 

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/33d21e38-cca2-11f1-b8ea-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26290607552722.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/33d21e38-cca2-11f1-b8ea-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26290607552722.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1a3de1ac-cca0-11f1-a0db-8911ee908170</guid><pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 16:50:49 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/33d21e38-cca2-11f1-b8ea-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26290607552722.jpg">© Laurent Cipriani, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Africa</category><title>More than 150 killed in Sudan drone strike on disputed Abyei border region</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/africa/20261020-more-than-150-killed-sudan-drone-strike-disputed-abyei-border-region</link><description>
At least 153 people have been killed in a drone strike on a market in the disputed Abyei region, where a fire at a nearby fuel depot continued to burn on Tuesday. Local officials blamed Sudan’s military for Monday’s attack, which also left dozens injured. 
 

 

 

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/06f56856-cc9e-11f1-acba-638c1c1f5fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/AP071212050372.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/06f56856-cc9e-11f1-acba-638c1c1f5fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/AP071212050372.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">46b3841a-cc9d-11f1-88ca-6b9c4a17bd3c</guid><pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 16:24:47 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/06f56856-cc9e-11f1-acba-638c1c1f5fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/AP071212050372.jpg">© Alfred de Montesquiou, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>France: Local curfews imposed after protests</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261020-france-local-curfews-imposed-after-protests</link><description>
French cities that imposed a curfew Monday saw a generally calm night, after October 17 protests devolved into violent riots this past weekend. Despite criticism from citizens, France's government said it is maintaining the measure where necessary on Tuesday night.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/39de51f0-cc9f-11f1-bc4d-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/title-3-1.jpeg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/39de51f0-cc9f-11f1-bc4d-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/title-3-1.jpeg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">58f0cd7a-cc9f-11f1-ba79-bd8ec08ef998</guid><pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 16:09:44 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>France's decades-long ties with Gulf states built on 'economic development, oil, defence agreements'</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261020-france-s-decades-long-ties-with-gulf-states-built-on-economic-development-oil-defense-agreements-1</link><description>
Genie Godula is pleased to welcome François Gouyette, former French ambassador to the UAE and Saudi Arabia. Against a backdrop of violent unrest at home and escalating conflict in the Middle East, French President Emmanuel Macron's Gulf diplomacy underscores the increasingly blurred boundaries between domestic economic security and international strategic commitments. Ambassador Gouyette argues that the visit serves a dual purpose: alleviating France's energy pressures while reaffirming its longstanding defense partnerships with Gulf monarchies. Insisting that "France has to play its role as a key partner," Gouyette portrays French military assistance as an expression of strategic solidarity rather than direct participation in the war with Iran. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/4d3474bc-cc97-11f1-b7a6-638c1c1f5fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261020-140836-141726-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/4d3474bc-cc97-11f1-b7a6-638c1c1f5fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261020-140836-141726-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">52e2169e-cc97-11f1-9953-d12189466dc0</guid><pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 15:52:47 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>US midterm elections: Trump approval rating falls to new low</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261020-us-midterm-elections-trump-approval-rating-falls-to-new-low</link><description>
With US President Donald Trump’s approval rating falling to a record low of 31%, Republicans are facing mounting concerns ahead of November’s midterm elections. Republicans are at risk of losing control of the House of Representatives, but how big could the Democrats’ gains be? FRANCE 24’s International Affairs Editor Kethevane Gorjestani explains.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/78964d88-cba7-11f1-83fd-638c1c1f5fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-17T212609Z-1651462827-RC285OA65KAS-RTRMADP-3-USA-TRUMP-KENTUCKY.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/78964d88-cba7-11f1-83fd-638c1c1f5fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-17T212609Z-1651462827-RC285OA65KAS-RTRMADP-3-USA-TRUMP-KENTUCKY.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">eb02ff9e-cc95-11f1-a33f-379da1eeb20b</guid><pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 15:22:29 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

<![CDATA[ Latest from Space.com ]]> https://www.space.com/feeds.xml Tue, 20 Oct 2026 18:00:00 +0000 en <![CDATA[ Jeff Bezos is playing the long game with Blue Origin (op-ed) ]]> Daniel Biedermann is a partner at NewSpace Capital. He contributed this article to Space.com's Expert Voices: Op-Ed & Insights.

Jeff Bezos, the founder and former CEO of Amazon, recently said that Blue Origin, his space technology company, is likely to go public in the coming years. The announcement has (unsurprisingly) attracted considerable attention, not least because Bezos has spent more than two decades financing the company largely from his personal wealth. He has invested billions of dollars in developing rockets, spacecraft and other forms of technology, often with very little prospect of an immediate return. But although Bezos has now raised the possibility of an initial public offering, he has given no firm indication of when one might happen. He may be right to keep his options open.

Bezos founded Blue Origin in 2000. Because he has financed so much of its development by himself, the company has been able to pursue ambitious engineering projects without the financial pressures that publicly listed businesses typically face. But developing reusable rockets, manufacturing spacecraft and building the infrastructure needed for future lunar missions requires extraordinary amounts of capital: These projects can take decades to complete, and even the wealthiest investors must think hard about how best to finance them over the long term. Bezos, then, has good reasons to seek additional sources of investment — particularly as Blue Origin prepares to expand its commercial operations.

An IPO would give Blue Origin the means to raise substantial capital from public investors and reduce its dependence on Bezos's personal wealth. The company could then use that money to expand manufacturing, develop new technology and compete for a greater share of the growing space market. Public ownership would also give existing investors the power to sell some of their holdings and could make it easier for Blue Origin to finance acquisitions. But the company would also have to meet the expectations of shareholders, who would expect to see regular evidence of commercial progress. This, I suspect, is why Bezos wants to establish a stronger business before committing to a listing.

It might have much to prove commercially, but Blue Origin’s technical progress has been remarkable. In January 2025, its New Glenn rocket reached orbit for the first time — a significant achievement for a vehicle built to compete in the heavy-lift launch market. The company has also secured government and commercial contracts and continued developing its lunar capabilities. But it will eventually have to demonstrate that it can launch New Glenn frequently, reliably and at a commercially competitive cost, and it is still some way away from that point.

Some will be asking whether Bezos wants to raise money to accelerate growth or simply to reduce the amount he himself must invest. Such doubts could affect the company's valuation and make it harder to attract investors who share its long-term ambitions. But again, this suggests Bezos is playing the long game. And given the enthusiasm that has surrounded some billionaire-led space ventures, this is sensible. Investors have sometimes attached extraordinary valuations to companies with ambitious plans but limited commercial experience. Space businesses certainly require ambition: engineers will often spend years developing technology before they can sell it. But investors have to distinguish between technical achievement and commercial performance. At the end of the day, they are seeking a strong rate of return.

What’s also worth considering is how Blue Origin's progress could benefit the wider space industry, particularly the specialist companies that supply technology to larger manufacturers and operators. SpaceX has achieved remarkable success in part by developing and manufacturing much of its technology internally. This includes its rockets, spacecraft and satellites. Blue Origin also does something similar, undertaking substantial engineering and manufacturing work itself, but it is not quite so vertically integrated, and thus may have greater scope to work with external suppliers as it expands. It already buys parts, equipment and services from hundreds of businesses. If it can successfully increase its production and launch activity, these suppliers could receive more orders and gain opportunities to develop new technologies. That’s to the good of the sector as a whole.

Why? Because a successful space industry needs more than a handful of large launch providers. It needs companies specializing in satellite communications, propulsion, electronics, software and other areas. Such businesses may have developed highly sophisticated products, but they need bigger customers and predictable demand to expand and produce more. Blue Origin could become an important customer for some of these, particularly if it chooses to buy specialist technology rather than make everything internally. Greater competition between the bigger space companies could translate to more potential customers for suppliers and fewer dependent commercial relationships.

Investors would benefit. There’s real potential in businesses that provide the technology and services on which larger space companies depend — the ‘picks and shovels.’ These can sometimes serve several customers and markets, making them less dependent on the success of a single program. A growing Blue Origin would create more opportunities for companies like these — although, of course, much will depend on how Bezos chooses to organize its supply chain. We shouldn’t assume that Blue Origin will become more open to external suppliers than its competitors, but the possibility is at least worth entertaining.

As it is, Bezos still faces substantial challenges. Blue Origin is not yet a commercially mature business. The company must increase its launch activity; it must demonstrate its reliability; and it must compete for customers in the public and private sectors. It must also decide how much technology to manufacture internally and whether and where third parties can provide better products or products at a lower cost. Bezos has the resources to give the company time to answer these questions, and he appears to be willing to use them. If he continues to prioritize commercial performance before pursuing an IPO, then Blue Origin could eventually enter the public markets in a much stronger position.

]]> <![CDATA[ A supercomputer is about to launch to the moon for the 1st time, aboard a rover named FLIP ]]> HAWTHORNE, Calif. — A moon buggy carrying a history-making supercomputer is ready to launch to the lunar surface. And it's taking some inspiration from Mars.

Later this year, Astrolab will launch its uncrewed moon rover FLIP to the lunar south pole as part of the Griffin Mission 1, or Griffin-1. The California company is one of two that NASA has selected to develop a drivable rover for the agency's Artemis program. On board FLIP will be Hewlett Packard Enterprise's (HPE) Spaceborne Computer-4, an advanced computer module built to be used in space.

This will be the first time that high-performance computing and artificial intelligence will be tested on the lunar surface. As NASA gets closer to landing humans back on the moon with Artemis, advancements like this aim to support future human habitation as well as economic activity on and around the moon.

"We're sending the first supercomputer from HPE to the lunar surface later this year, doing the first GPU [graphics processing unit] on the moon [and the] first AI experiments on the moon," Jaret Matthews, founder and CEO of Astrolab, said during an Oct. 14 media event here at Astrolab's headquarters. "They're breaking new ground, and they're ahead of the curve."

The computer is designed to be lightweight, compact, self-contained and fanless. It has a low-power 64-bit CPU (central processing unit) with a GPU. The computer will be attached to FLIP's cooling system and will be powered by a system supported by both batteries and solar cells on the rover. The computer will also be paired with solid state drives from the company KIOXIA that will allow for memory storage.

So, what will a supercomputer and AI accomplish on this uncrewed mission? First and foremost, the flightwill test how the computer works in this extreme environment. The computer is built with heat-conductive aluminum and is designed with the specific conditions of the lunar south pole in mind. But while it was designed and tested to be able to withstand the extreme temperatures and conditions on the moon's surface, the upcoming mission seeks to show that this advanced technology can actually work in this environment.

"NASA's given us a real challenge," Matthews told Space.com at the media event. "We have to design for a full year on the lunar surface. So that means surviving multiple lunar nights, upwards of 150 hours of complete darkness where we're not receiving energy or warmth from the sun. And then, also, there's going to be a long period [in] which we're operating semi-autonomously for [when] the astronauts are not there … and so we're having to develop a semi-autonomous platform that will spend many months [and] travel hundreds of kilometers [on the moon]."

But the computer will more than just prove its durability, if all goes to plan. It will also analyze visual data captured on the mission and enable autonomous observations, process navigation, mapping and terrain analysis. The mission also promises to test AI capabilities, though it's unclear what exact applications we'll see with this lunar AI. HPE shared in a statement that "an AI services container will demonstrate reliable deployment of scalable AI service applications on the moon."

It is also to be determined exactly how, once tested, these capabilities might be used with future crewed missions. Astronauts aboard the International Space Station already use computers for communications, science experiments and other daily tasks while living in space, but we can't say yet exactly how future astronauts might use these capabilities, especially with the addition of AI, on the moon.

From Mars to the moon

One interesting aspect of this new development is where it came from. While HPE has provided computing power to NASA for decades, Matthews is also bringing his previous experience working at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) into this new venture.

"One of the experiments [that will be] running on the spaceborne computer on the moon is a localization software experiment from JPL. It has been used on Mars, and this will be the first time it's used on the moon," Matthews said.

"The challenge with the moon and Mars is that there's no GPS, so locating yourself and knowing where you are on the surface [can be difficult]," he added. "So we're going to be running what is essentially a machine learning algorithm that JPL developed to take a map that's stored in memory … and compare it to the local terrain we see around us, and then do a match. So essentially, match features of the local terrain to the map that's stored in memory to help find ourselves on the map and keep ourselves away from dangerous craters."

As its name suggests, Griffin-1 will be the first mission for the robotic Griffin moon lander, which was developed by Astrobotic. The Pittsburgh company is flying Griffin-1 for NASA, under the agency's CLPS (Commercial Lunar Payload Services) program. In addition to FLIP, the mission will carry Astrobiotic's CubeRover, a small, uncrewed rover; LandCam-X, an optical navigation system; and Nanofiche GLPH (Galactic Library to Preserve Humanity), a tiny archive of human history, to the moon's surface.

"The moon presents a challenging environment for advanced computing, and we’re pleased to provide HPE with an opportunity to demonstrate its technology on the lunar surface," Matthews added in a statement. "Our FLIP rover is designed to accommodate a variety of payloads, and this mission will demonstrate how commercial lunar mobility platforms can support technology development and scientific research."

]]> <![CDATA[ Red light, white light: How to preserve your night vision while using stargazing apps ]]> The best stargazing apps can take your observation of the night sky to the next level, whether that's using augmented reality (AR mode) to identify stars or looking up the next lunar eclipse.

However, the bright light emitted by smartphone screens can prevent your eyes from adjusting to the dark. If you're using one of the best telescopes, you'll want to preserve your night vision even more. Fortunately, there are ways to all but eliminate this problem.

Why are bright screens bad for stargazing?

When you step out into the dark, it can take up to 20-30 minutes for your vision to adjust. The rod cells in your eyes build up a chemical known as rhodopsin, which gives you night vision.

However, bright light bleaches that chemical, negatively impacting your night vision. So when you look through a telescope, binoculars or just turn your eyes to the night sky after peering at a bright phone screen, it'll be harder for you to pick out fainter objects such as galaxies and nebulas.

One way of fixing this problem is simply to put your phone away and wait another 20-30 minutes. But if you're using a stargazing app to help you navigate the night skies, that's not really an option.

The good news is that, between individual stargazing apps and your phone's own built-in features, you can minimize the impact of your smartphone's screen light.

How to block white light in stargazing apps

Many of the best stargazing apps will let you enable a red light filter or similar, though this option may not always be present in the free version. Here's how to do that in three of our favorite stargazing apps:

SkyView: Tap the screen, tap the horizontal lines, tap on Settings, then Display, then Night Mode and Red.

Star Walk 2: Tap the horizontal lines, tap on Settings, then tap the button next to Night Mode.

Sky Tonight: Tap the horizontal lines, tap on Settings, then Tools, then Night Mode.

All these modes will minimize the amount of white light coming from the app. However, be aware that this is only within the app. Once you go back to your phone's main menu, it will be at full color. With the red screen naturally looking darker, you may have turned up the brightness on your phone, so making the switch away from the app will be quite the shock.

If you want to dim your whole phone or put it into red light mode, here's how to do that on Android or iPhone.

How to block white light on Android phones

On Android, there are several ways to minimize the impact of bright light, depending on the model and make of phone you have.

One near-universal option is to dim your smartphone. Swipe down the notification panel from the top of the screen and you'll see a brightness slider. Slide this to the left to dim your phone.

We'd also recommend disabling adaptive brightness in the Display section of your phone's settings. You may also have an Extra Dim option in the Accessibility menu — just don't dim the screen to the point of not being able to see it at all!

Some Android phones, such as recent Samsung and Google Pixel models, also offer a Red Filter. On some, you'll find this in Accessibility, then Vision Enhancements, then Color Filter. You can then choose the color you want and also tweak the opacity.

All the above options will let you continue to use your smartphone for stargazing, while minimizing its negative impact on your night vision.

How to block white light on Apple iPhones

As with Android phones, iPhones have a built-in option to dim the screen brightness. In this case, you swipe down from the top of the screen and look for the vertical brightness slider, represented by a sun icon. Reduce the slider as much as you're comfortable with, dimming the screen while still keeping it visible.

Beyond that, recent iPhones also offer the ability to apply a color filter, again via their Accessibility options. Here's how to do that.

First, tap on the Settings icon, then pick Accessibility. Select Display & Text Size and go to Color Filters. Tap the Color Filter button. Then, pick Color Tint and move the Hue and Intensity sliders all the way to the right.

]]> <![CDATA[ The view from the edge of a sparkling spiral galaxy | Space photo of the day for Oct. 20, 2026 ]]>

If you were approaching the edge of a spiral galaxy, arriving from afar through the cosmos, it might look something like this.

What is it?

In this new snapshot by the Hubble Space Telescope's Advanced Camera for Surveys (ACS), we can see the edge of the spiral galaxy NGC 1827. Found about 37 million light-years from Earth, this galaxy sparkles in this side-on view.

Not all spiral galaxies are the same. This galaxy is what is known as an "intermediate" spiral, which means that its structure sits somewhere between that of a barred and unbarred spiral galaxy. Barred galaxies have a distinctive central, bar-shaped structure, while the unbarred variety lacks this bar and can look more like circular spirals.

NGC 1827's spiral shape isn't clear from the side, however. From this perspective, we see its twinkling edge, speckled with stars and woven together with brown ribbons of dust.

Why is it incredible?

Beneath the beauty of this spiral edge lies an expansive, cosmic landscape. Bright blue stars dot the spiral's side, with one particularly luminous star taking the spotlight with four diffraction spikes — created by light bending through the inner workings of Hubble's camera — emanating from its center.

This image was captured as part of a larger Hubble survey that's exploring 260 satellite galaxies, which are galaxies gravitationally bound to larger hosts. Hubble is specifically looking to survey satellite galaxies that lie near host galaxies similar to our own Milky Way.

So far, Hubble has spotted 111 such satellites and will continue to observe, hunting for the rest.

By studying satellite galaxies like this one, which also happens to be an especially low-mass galaxy, researchers could better understand the complicated dynamics both within the galaxies themselves and between them and their host galaxies.

]]> <![CDATA[ Could a $200K bond for satellites paid before launch prevent a space junk disaster in orbit? Here's why some scientists think so ]]> The space around Earth is turning into a junkyard. Researchers think a refundable deposit scheme could force satellite operators to clean up their act before a tipping point is reached.

For years, space sustainability experts have warned that the growing number of satellites in orbit and the quantity of dead metal left behind threatens to trigger a dangerous cascade of collisions known as the Kessler Syndrome. Predicted in the 1970s by NASA physicist Donald Kessler, this chain of orbital smashups could make the space around Earth unusable and unsafe.

The dangerous tipping might be nearer than some think. Humankind's utilization of space is at an inflection point, as companies such as SpaceX, Blue Origin and Amazon plan to launch constellations of hundreds of thousands of telecommunication satellites and orbiting data centers in the coming years.

"Low Earth orbit looks like lots of other resources that we have trashed as economic actors," Daniel Kaffine, a professor of environmental and resource economics at University of Colorado Boulder, told Space.com.

"Waiting until it gets really, really bad to start implementing any of these types of policy interventions has historically been what we have done," Kaffine added. "But maybe we can think about things we can do right now."

In a paper published last month in the journal Nature Communications, Kaffine and his collaborators propose a scheme that would require satellite operators to post a bond of $200,000 before launch, refundable with interest upon the completion of a successful deorbit. Companies that fail to remove their junk would lose the money, which could go toward a shared pool funding active debris-removal missions, the researchers said.

"You could possibly raise billions of dollars by that," said Kaffine. "We think it's a very neat policy that doesn't require international coordination."

International bodies, such as the Inter-Agency Space Debris Coordination Committee, ask satellite operators to remove their spacecraft from orbit within 25 years after the mission's end. The American Federal Communications Commission (FCC) imposes an even stricter standard — a five-year requirement for satellites in low Earth orbit. Still, a staggering 60% of satellites remain in place when their propellant runs out, the researchers say, as no consequences ensue if they fail to deorbit.

Solving the problem on the international level would be difficult, as international bodies have no powers to enforce compliance. Moreover, the United Nations Committee on the Peaceful Uses of Outer Space (COPUOS), which sets down rules for the peaceful exploration of outer space, requires the unanimous support of every member state to pass new regulations, which is nearly impossible to achieve.

"The policy we propose could be implemented on a national level, which is why we think it's interesting," Indigo Brownhall, a space sustainability researcher at University College London and the paper's lead author, told Space.com. "Any country in Europe can request satellites registered with them to follow this bond policy."

To put it simply, no satellite registered in a given country gets to space before putting the money into the kitty. The researchers acknowledge that it might be hard to persuade major players historically averse to regulations, such as the U.S., to roll out such a scheme. But they say a more environmentally conscious block, like the European Union (EU), could enforce compliance by limiting market access to those who observe their rules.

"The consumer market in Europe is massive, like 300 to 400 million people," Brownhall said. "And the EU can request anyone who wants to sell space data or any products in the EU to follow their rules. They did this with GDPR [General Data Protection Regulation]. And you can imagine that somebody like Starlink [SpaceX's satellite-internet subsidiary] surely wants to sell Starlink terminals to Europeans."

The authors estimate that, even if the scheme only covered 20% of global satellite launches, it would reduce the number of derelict satellites careening around the planet by 18%.

Currently, more than 57,000 pieces of space debris larger than 4 inches (10 centimeters) hurtle around Earth completely out of control, according to estimates by the European Space Agency. That's double the figure from less than 10 years ago. Most of these fragments were generated by explosions and orbital collisions that shattered satellites and used rocket stages into clouds of dangerous debris.

"Leaving big satellites that no longer work up there is like a ticking time bomb," Brownhall said. "Active satellites can move out of the way, but when two derelict satellites are going to hit each other, there is nothing you can do but watch it."

Kaffine said the policy could be modelled on U.S. oil operators' bond scheme, in place since the 1960s, which ensures that oil giants plug used oil wells after ceasing extraction.

"If the oil operators clean up after completing the oil production job, they get the money back," said Kaffine. "If they don't, the money goes into a fund, which the government then uses to clean up orphan wells. It's quite an analogous situation to what we see in space."

In the meantime, evidence of the worsening orbital situation is coming thick and fast. Space situational awareness companies such as U.S.-based LeoLabs, which use networks of ground-based radars and telescopes to monitor traffic in space, report increasing numbers of disintegration events — incidents involving either an explosion or a collision between old satellites, fragments and rocket bodies. In the past six months, LeoLabs has reported at least four fragmentation events in space, which together created hundreds of new pieces of space debris.

]]> <![CDATA[ SpaceX launches its 'Starfall' return capsule for 2nd time ever (video) ]]>

SpaceX just launched its mysterious "Starfall" return capsule for the second time ever.

Starfall was one of 32 payloads on the company's Bandwagon-5 rideshare mission, which launched atop a Falcon 9 rocket at 7:04 a.m. EDT (1104 GMT) today (Oct. 20) from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida.

SpaceX has been relatively quiet about Starfall, which debuted this past June on a Falcon 9 launch from the Cape.

That June 23 flight was a dedicated demonstration mission for Starfall, designed to show that the capsule can fly in a controlled fashion and survive the harrowing downward trip through Earth's atmosphere.

And those will be Starfall's main jobs. The vehicle "will enable affordable, routine access to the microgravity environment for scientific research and in-space manufacturing," SpaceX in a June 23 X post, one of the few public statements the company has made about Starfall.

Indeed, most of the details that we have about the capsule come from an environmental assessment that was published by the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration in May.

According to that document, the disk-shaped Starfall is roughly 2.5 feet (0.75 meters) tall and 10.2 feet (3.1 m) wide. It weighs about 4,600 pounds (2,100 kilograms) and can bring 2,200 pounds (1,000 kg) of payload back down to Earth.

Starfall wasn't the only return capsule that went up on Bandwagon-5. Among the other 31 payloads on the flight was W-Series 7, the latest orbital "mini-factory" built and operated by the California company Varda Space Industries.

The W-Series capsules are designed to both host the production of valuable goods such as pharmaceuticals and bring them safely down to Earth, Varda has said.

The other payloads on Bandwagon-5 are a mix of "cubesats and microsats," according to SpaceX's mission description. Among the latter is Pelican-12, a sharp-eyed Earth-observation satellite built by the San Francisco company Planet.

The 32 payloads were deployed over a two-hour span beginning about 57 minutes after launch. Starfall will be the last to separate, releasing from the Falcon 9's upper stage two hours and 48 minutes post-liftoff.

The Falcon 9's first stage, meanwhile, came back to Earth as planned on Bandwagon-5. It touched down about nine minutes after launch, coming down in the Atlantic Ocean atop the SpaceX drone ship "A Shortfall of Gravitas." It was the 19th mission for this particular booster, according to the company.

Bandwagon is one of two SpaceX rideshare programs. The other, known as Transporter, has been busier, flying 18 missions to date.

The first Transporter mission, which lifted off in January 2021, delivered 143 payloads to Earth orbit, a single-launch record that still stands.

]]> <![CDATA[ NASA closes the book on epic OSIRIS-REx asteroid-sampling mission: 'I am immensely proud of what we did' ]]> On Sept. 30, NASA formally concluded OSIRIS-REx, the historic first U.S. mission to pluck a pristine piece of an asteroid and deliver it safely back to Earth.

The van-sized OSIRIS-REx spacecraft — whose name is short for Origins, Spectral Interpretation, Resource Identification, Security-Regolith Explorer — visited and sampled Bennu, an ancient space rock holding pristine remnants from the dawn of our solar system more than 4.5 billion years ago. Among those cosmic relics are raw organic building blocks, the kind that may have seeded life on Earth.

"I have known this day was coming for a long time, but it is still difficult to see it arrive," OSIRIS-REx Principal Investigator Dante Lauretta, who's based at the University of Arizona, said in a post on LinkedIn. "I feel enormous pride in what we accomplished together, and real sadness that this journey has come to an end."

For the mission team, the farewell capped a decade of high-stakes engineering, on-the-fly troubleshooting and nail-biting close calls that ultimately delivered to Earth the largest asteroid sample ever collected in space, one that held secrets from the early solar system.

Long before launch, the team faced obstacles that nearly thwarted the endeavor — chiefly, two rejections from NASA — before finally securing the green light for the $1 billion project under the New Frontiers Program in 2011.

When OSIRIS-REx launched on Sept. 8, 2016, on a two-year journey across the inner solar system, Bennu was little more than a point of light in telescopes. Scientists expected the asteroid’s surface to be a smooth, sandy sphere where OSIRIS-REx could seamlessly touch down. Much to their surprise, however, when the probe arrived at the asteroid in late 2018, it revealed Bennu to be a treacherous, loosely bound amalgamation of jagged boulders.

"Our expectations about the asteroid's surface were completely wrong," Lauretta said in an Oct. 7 statement from the University of Arizona. "There was no obvious place to collect a sample anywhere."

When OSIRIS-REx touched down on a small crater named Nightingale, Bennu offered so little structural resistance that scientists said its surface reacted more like fluid than a hard, rocky shell. The spacecraft's sampling head sank directly into the asteroid, stopping after burrowing 20 inches (51 centimeters) deep by firing its thrusters at the right time to pull away, with the precious sample in hand.

Then came another nail-biting moment: The sample collector lid got jammed in a partially open position because so much material was scooped up, allowing fragments of the precious cargo to escape. In a race against time to prevent further loss, the mission team quickly stowed the sampler head directly inside the return capsule, securing the cosmic treasure for its journey back to Earth.

Even the final return to Earth, on Sept. 24, 2023, kept the team on edge: A parachute failed to deploy properly during reentry, forcing a tense but ultimately safe landing in the Utah desert.

"Successful exploration missions are not those that avoid surprises; they are those that are deliberately designed to adapt to them," Lauretta said in the statement, quoting a line from the mission's final report to NASA.

"That certainly describes OSIRIS-REx," he said. "Again and again, the mission presented us with circumstances we had not expected, and again and again, this team found a way forward."

]]> <![CDATA[ The X-Files Lego set is a wonderful bit of 90s sci-fi nostalgia ]]> Millennials get a lot of flak for being overly nostalgic, but I don't think that's fair. When the modern-day world has nothing to offer us but AI slop, shrinkflation and a sad acceptance that we can't be bothered to do anything about global warming. It's easy to see why we yearn for the days of Pogs, the Backstreet Boys, and Saved by the Bell.

One area that we definitely had it good in the 90s was sci-fi, when legendary shows like Star Trek: The Next Generation, Stargate SG-1, and — of course — The X-Files ruled our TV screens long before the age of streaming services. You can relive those glory days of alien conspiracies, spooky happenings and cell phones the size of a brick with the Lego Ideas The X-Files set.

This 1478 piece set is essentially two dioramas crammed into a single display piece. The top of the model depicts a spinning UFO floating above one of those iconic coniferous forests that dominated 90s sci-fi. Why? Because — thanks to some generous tax credits — it was cheaper to shoot in Vancouver, so that's where they all flocked.

Disney Plus / Hulu bundle: was $12.99 now $11.99
Catch Mulder and Scully in every season of The X-Files on Hulu, which is available bundled with Disney+ for only $11.99/month for the first six months, then increasing to $12.99/month.View Deal

Beneath the woodland scene, though, is the real star of the show: Mulder's office, squirrelled away in the basement of the FBI's J. Edgar Hoover Building in Washington, D.C. This dingy little office is where Scully meets "Spooky Mulder", kicking off a glorious sci-fi odyssey that would last for eleven seasons (and two movies).

Mulder's dingy little base of operations has been stunningly recreated here, with both overt references and subtle nods that X-Files fans will appreciate. The iconic "I want to believe" poster adorns the wall, alongside photographs of crop circles and a newspaper clipping from a paper called "The Lone Brickman" — a nice nod to "The Lone Gunmen". There's even an actual X-File sitting on the desk, and a cute Lego spoof of the "Face on Mars", with a photo on the wall that shows a Lego head on the moon.

The X-Files Complete Boxset: $160
Prefer to actually own your media? Make your way through this X-Files Complete Boxset on DVD. Just bear in mind that you will need a region-free DVD player to watch it with.

It's been a hot minute since I watched The X-Files (that DVD box set beside my TV is calling to me), but even so, I had a blast building my way down memory lane, remembering episodes as I assembled the diorama. I love the little touches, like the display cabinets filled with artifacts, the VHS tapes scattered around the office and the black oil spillage on the floor.

As with most Lego sets, the minifigures are half the joy. You get Mulder and Scully, obviously, with the dynamic duo of FBI agents both rocking flashlights (no smartphones with built-in lights back in the 90s). Mulder is wearing dark blue, while Scully is rocking an orangey brown suit, with both of them sporting an FBI badge.

Outside of the principal pair, you also get Skinner, Mr X, and the Cigarette Smoking Man. Mulder's partner-turned-nemesis Alex Krycek also gets a suitably devious-looking minifig. It's the gloves, they just make him look like a bad man (which, to be fair, he is). Finally, to ramp up the paranormal scale, we also get a pair of monster minifigs: a grey alien and Flukeman minifigures. The grey alien was a must-have, especially given the UFO floating atop this display piece, but the one-off monster of the week, Flukeman, felt like a weird choice.

Also, this John Doggett erasure will not stand. Sure, he could never replace Mulder, but Robert Patrick's seasons eight and nine run was excellent and he deserved a spot here.

And while I'm voicing minor gripes, the usual Lego FOMO tricks were in force with this set; if you pre-ordered, you got an exclusive gift set — Scully's Lab — free of charge. This extra little diorama isn't necessary, but it does feel like the collection is incomplete without it and it's not for sale separately, so you'll have to try your luck with eBay scalpers if you want it.

Speaking of Scully, Gillian Anderson has stated that after season 11 wrapped in 2018, she was done with the role. That wasn't entirely accurate, though, as she donned the lab gloves one more time for the Lego X-Files set advert. It's a short bit of fan service, but a nice touch, and, once again, it sparks those 90s neurons.

All these delicious Member Berries come at a price, though, and that's the price. This blast from the past will set you back $199 (£179 in the UK). That's no small chunk of change. But then again, anyone who wants this set is in their thirties or forties and can probably afford that outlay for the nostalgia trip. And look at it this way: when The X-Files debuted back in 1993, the price would only have been about $86.

I had a great time building the Lego X-Files set and if you're a fan of the series, you will too. Nostalgia often feels like a cheat code to our hearts, but there's nothing wrong with that. We deserve to remember the good times and the truth is that The X-Files was about as good as it ever got for sci-fi fans.

You can buy the Lego X-Files set now, available for $199/£179 from the Lego store.

]]> <![CDATA[ Japan launches historic MMX sample-return mission to Mars' moon Phobos (video) ]]>

Japan's groundbreaking mission to Mars is officially underway, headed to the Red Planet's mysterious moons Phobos and Deimos for a historic sample-return attempt.

The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission launched today (Oct. 19) from Tanegashima Space Center in Japan, riding an H3 rocket that lifted off from Pad-2 at Tanegashima's Yoshinobu Launch Complex at 3:41 p.m. EDT (1941 GMT; 4:41 a.m. local time in Japan on Oct. 20).

The JAXA (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency)-led MMX mission is bound for Mars orbit, where it will study the planet's two moons, Phobos and Deimos. If everything goes according to plan, MMX will become the first spacecraft to land on and return samples from Phobos for study back on Earth, which scientists think could shed light on a decades-old mystery about the moons' origins and reveal clues about the formation of the early solar system.

It was the 10th liftoff of Japan's expendable, two-stage H3 rocket, which was jointly developed by JAXA and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries. After clearing its launch pad today, the 207-foot-tall (63 meters) launch vehicle flew a nominal trajectory through its ascent corridor over the Pacific Ocean, jettisoning its four solid boosters in pairs just before the flight clock reached two minutes. The rocket shed its payload fairings about one minute and 20 seconds later, exposing MMX to the vacuum of space for the first time.

H3's first stage, powered by two LE-9 rocket engines, channels a mixture of liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen to produce a combined thrust of 331,000 pounds (1,471 kN), according to Mitsubishi Heavy Industries. As the mission clock approached T+5 minutes, H3 executed its main engine cutoff procedure and separated from the second stage, which ignited its engines for a 5.5-minute burn about 10 seconds later.

All continued to go to plan after that. The H3's upper stage ignited its engine for a second time for a trans-Mars injection burn about one hour and four minutes after liftoff, a maneuver that lasted roughly six minutes and 25 seconds and took MMX to a maximum velocity of about 24,145 mph (38,858 kph).

MMX was released from the rocket's upper stage right on schedule, about one minute after the completion of that burn and roughly 71 minutes after liftoff. The success elicited loud cheers in mission control, which viewers saw and heard on JAXA's launch webcast.

MMX is now under its own power, and on course for Mars. The interplanetary transit will last about 10 months, with the spacecraft scheduled to arrive at the Red Planet in August 2027. When it does, MMX's propulsion module will execute an orbital insertion burn to place itself in a quasi-satellite orbit (QSO) around Phobos, which places MMX within the space around the moon as both circle Mars.

MMX will spend about three years in the Martian system, devoting much of that time to studying the 14-mile-wide (22 km) Phobos with its science instruments. The spacecraft also carries the IDEFIX rover, a joint effort of the space agencies of France and Germany, which is scheduled to deploy to the surface of Phobos in late 2028 or early 2029.

After a mapping campaign to select suitable landing sites, MMX will perform two separate touchdowns on Phobos to collect and stow samples in the spacecraft's return capsule. Following its second landing and sample collection, MMX will briefly return to QSO with Phobos before transferring to a more elongated orbit around Mars that intersects with the planet's smaller moon, Deimos, which is just 8 miles (14 km) in diameter.

During the last several months of its time around Mars, MMX will perform a series of Deimos flybys before departing for Earth in November 2030. If all goes according to plan, the MMX sample-return capsule will land in Australia in 2031.

Scientists are counting on those samples, and other data collected during MMX's time around Mars, to answer a decades-old question surrounding the Martian moons' origins. Competing theories and conflicting evidence point to two possibilities for how Mars got its moons.

Their near-circular, equatorial orbits suggest a narrative similar to how Earth's moon is thought to have formed — as a result of a massive planetary impact between Mars and some other giant space rock, which broke off pieces of the planet that eventually coalesced to form the natural satellites that orbit there today.

Neither Phobos nor Deimos is spherical, isntead; both are oblong and lumpy, like potatoes. That fact — along with their chemical composition, as far as we have been able to tell using telescopic spectroscopy — point to the possibility that Phobos and Deimos were asteroids from the early solar system that were captured by Mars' gravitational pull. Figuring out the moons' true origin story would provide key clues about Mars' geological past, the solar system's early history and the formation of the inner planets, mission team members have said.

Once the MMX samples are safely returned to Earth, scientists will study their composition and mineralogy, then compare such chemical fingerprints with those of Martian rocks and asteroid material. These analyses, combined with data collected by MMX during its mission, will help nail down the origin of Phobos — and by extension, Deimos. — by

While JAXA leads MMX, the mission is an international effort, with interagency partnerships between JAXA, NASA and the European Space Agency (ESA), as well as U.S. and European companies, which supplied a handful of the spacecraft's scientific hardware and communications equipment.

NASA's contributions to MMX include the Mars-moon Exploration with Gamma rays and Neutrons (MEGANE, pronounced "meh-gah-nay") device, which is a gamma-ray and neutron spectrometer built by the Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory (APL); a Honeybee Robotics-built pneumatic sampler; and communications support using the agency's Deep Space Network.

NASA has also invested approximately $87 million through the end of the mission, which includes funding for United States scientists and astromaterials experts on the MMX team. The agency is getting something concrete for such contributions: At least 15% of the planned 10-gram (0.35 ounces) returned Phobos sample will be reserved for NASA's study. Those materials will be transferred and maintained at the agency's Johnson Space Center in Houston for analysis and long-term preservation.

MMX is not the first Phobos sample-return project to take flight, by the way. That distinction goes to Russia's Phobos-Grunt ("Phobos-Soil") mission, which launched in November 2011 but failed to get out of Earth orbit due to a rocket glitch. The 14.5-ton spacecraft eventually crashed back to Earth over the Pacific Ocean in January 2012.

Editor's note: This story was updated at 5 p.m. ET on Oct. 19 with news of MMX's successful separation from the H3 rocket's upper stage.

The spacecraft also carries the IDEFIX rover, a joint effort of the space agencies of France and Germany, which is scheduled to deploy to the surface of Phobos in late 2028 or early 2029.

After a mapping campaign to select suitable landing sites, MMX will perform two separate touchdowns on Phobos to collect and stow samples in the spacecraft's return capsule. Following its second landing and sample collection, MMX will briefly return to QSO with Phobos before transferring to a more elongated orbit around Mars that intersects with the planet's smaller moon, Deimos, which is just 8 miles (14 km) in diameter.

During the last several months of its time around Mars, MMX will perform a series of Deimos flybys before departing for Earth in November 2030. If all goes according to plan, the MMX sample-return capsule will land in Australia in 2031.

Scientists are counting on those samples, and other data collected during MMX's time around Mars, to answer a decades-old question surrounding the Martian moons' origins. Competing theories and conflicting evidence point to two possibilities for how Mars got its moons.

Their near-circular, equatorial orbits suggest a narrative similar to how Earth's moon is thought to have formed — as a result of a massive planetary impact between Mars and some other giant space rock, which broke off pieces of the planet that eventually coalesced to form the natural satellites that orbit there today.

Neither Phobos nor Deimos is spherical, isntead; both are oblong and lumpy, like potatoes. That fact — along with their chemical composition, as far as we have been able to tell using telescopic spectroscopy — point to the possibility that Phobos and Deimos were asteroids from the early solar system that were captured by Mars' gravitational pull. Figuring out the moons' true origin story would provide key clues about Mars' geological past, the solar system's early history and the formation of the inner planets, mission team members have said.

Once the MMX samples are safely returned to Earth, scientists will study their composition and mineralogy, then compare such chemical fingerprints with those of Martian rocks and asteroid material. These analyses, combined with data collected by MMX during its mission, will help nail down the origin of Phobos — and by extension, Deimos. — by

While JAXA leads MMX, the mission is an international effort, with interagency partnerships between JAXA, NASA and the European Space Agency (ESA), as well as U.S. and European companies, which supplied a handful of the spacecraft's scientific hardware and communications equipment.

NASA's contributions to MMX include the Mars-moon Exploration with Gamma rays and Neutrons (MEGANE, pronounced "meh-gah-nay") device, which is a gamma-ray and neutron spectrometer built by the Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory (APL); a Honeybee Robotics-built pneumatic sampler; and communications support using the agency's Deep Space Network.

NASA has also invested approximately $87 million through the end of the mission, which includes funding for United States scientists and astromaterials experts on the MMX team. The agency is getting something concrete for such contributions: At least 15% of the planned 10-gram (0.35 ounces) returned Phobos sample will be reserved for NASA's study. Those materials will be transferred and maintained at the agency's Johnson Space Center in Houston for analysis and long-term preservation.

MMX is not the first Phobos sample-return project to take flight, by the way. That distinction goes to Russia's Phobos-Grunt ("Phobos-Soil") mission, which launched in November 2011 but failed to get out of Earth orbit due to a rocket glitch. The 14.5-ton spacecraft eventually crashed back to Earth over the Pacific Ocean in January 2012.

Editor's note: This story was updated at 5 p.m. ET on Oct. 19 with news of MMX's successful separation from the H3 rocket's upper stage.

]]>

   <title>Obor budoucnosti. Českolipští ekologové získávají zkušenosti i za hranicemi</title>
   <link>https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/zpravy-region/obor-budoucnosti-ceskolipsti-ekologove-ziskavaji-zkusenosti-i-za-hranicemi/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=zpravy-region</link>
   <description>Jak vypadá moderní ekologie v praxi? Odpověď našli studenti maturitního oboru Ekologie a životní prostředí SZŠ a SOŠ Česká Lípa během odborné exkurze do německého Zwickau. Město, které dokázalo propojit průmyslovou tradici s moderními ekologickými technologiemi, se stalo inspirací pro všechny, kteří chtějí svou budoucnost spojit s ochranou přírody a udržitelným rozvojem.</description>

  <item>
   <title>Ruský satelit se přiblížil k družici pomáhající Ukrajině. Mohlo jít o špionáž</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/svet/rusky-satelit-se-priblizil-k-druzici-pomahajici-ukrajine-mohlo-jit-o-spionaz/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=svet</link>
   <description>Ruská družice Kosmos 2612 se přiblížila na stovky metrů ke komerční družici Iceye-X36, která pořizuje radarové snímky Země a může sloužit i k podpoře ukrajinské armády. Podle odborníků jde o bezprecedentní případ přiblížení jednoho vesmírného objektu k druhému bez svolení jeho provozovatelů. Záměr ruské strany zůstává nejasný.</description>

   <title>Jízdné v Libereckém kraji zdraží. Bankovní kartou už lidé výhodněji nezaplatí</title>
   <link>https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/zpravy-region/jizdne-v-libereckem-kraji-zdrazi-bankovni-kartou-uz-lide-vyhodneji-nezaplati/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=zpravy-region</link>
   <description>Cestující v Libereckém kraji čeká od ledna 2027 několik změn v integrovaném dopravním systému IDOL. Rozšíří se možnosti cestování za hranice, upraví se tarif u některých krátkých jízd a nově se změní také zvýhodnění podle způsobu placení. Ceny jízdného se zvýší v průměru o dvě procenta, za roční síťovou jízdenku lidé nově zaplatí 12 tisíc korun.</description>

   <title>Zpěvák Marcel Zmožek končí kariéru. Má vážné problémy, rodina zveřejnila vzkaz</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/kultura/zpevak-marcel-zmozek-konci-karieru-psychicke-problemy/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=kultura</link>
   <description>Český zpěvák, skladatel a textař Marcel Zmožek oznámil konec své hudební kariéry. Důvodem jsou závažné zdravotní potíže související s duševním onemocněním. Oznámila to jeho rodina na sociálních sítích a požádala fanoušky o pochopení a respektování soukromí.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Diskuse o Ukrajině bez Ukrajiny není možná, řekl v Oslu Zelenskyj</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/zahranicni/ukrajina-rusko-valka-usa-dohoda-mir-zelenskyj-trump.A261020_194307_zahranicni_dtt#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Diskuse o Ukrajině se nemůže konat bez Ukrajiny, zdůraznil v úterý ukrajinský prezident Volodymyr Zelenskyj k možné trojstranné schůzce USA, Ruska a Číny, kterou navrhl ruský prezident Vladimir Putin. Ukrajina je podle Zelenského Spojeným státům vděčná za obnovené sdílení zpravodajských informací a včasných varování před ruskými raketovými útoky.</description>
      <pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 18:13:48 GMT</pubDate>

    <item>
      <title>Zakáže zákon prodej živých ryb? Pospíšil to navrhl do zákona na ochranu zvířat</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/snemovna-zakon-na-ochranu-zvirad-proti-tyrani-zakaz-lovu-norovanin.A261020_045902_domaci_kop#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Zakáží poslanci, aby si lidé před Vánoci přinesli domů živého kapra a zabili ho až při přípravě štědrovečerního menu? Jiří Pospíšil, poslanec a první místopředseda TOP 09, předložil ve Sněmovně návrh, aby živé ryby určené ke konzumaci musely být před prodejem koncovému spotřebiteli usmrceny. </description>

    <item>
      <title>Rabují pitomci. Francie se učí tvrdou lekci o své bezvýznamnosti, míní politolog</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/zahranicni/francie-protesty-policie-sobota-pariz-demonstrace.A261020_100543_zahranicni_jhr#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Francouzské protesty doprovázené rabováním a ničením nejsou v zásadě ničím novým, jen prohloubí stávající polarizaci, uvádí profesor politologie z Pařížského institutu politických věd Sciences Po Jan Rovný. Podotýká, že vláda je široce nepopulární a její možnosti řešit situaci jsou omezené. Francie se podle něj těžce vyrovnává se skutečností, že už není světovou velmocí. </description>
      <pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 18:00:00 GMT</pubDate>

    <item>
      <title>Anketu Strom čtvrtstoletí vyhrál 400 let starý dub ze zámecké aleje na Přerovsku</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/olomouc/zpravy/stromem-ctvrtstoleti-dub-ze-skalicky-na-prerovsku-vyhral-v-ankete.A261020_192157_olomouc-zpravy_sahu#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Dub letní ze zámecké aleje ve Skaličce na Přerovsku se stal Stromem čtvrtstoletí. Rozhodli o tom lidé, kteří se zapojili do hlasování ve stejnojmenné anketě, kterou pořádala Nadace Partnerství. Dub, kterému je přibližně 400 let, získal 5727 hlasů. Nadace anketu o Strom čtvrtstoletí vyhlásila při 25. výročí soutěže Strom roku.</description>

<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/evropsti-operatori-se-spojuji-chteji-zdejsi-verzi-starlinku-ma-prinest-nezavislost-na-usa/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Čtyři největ&#353;í evrop&#353;tí telekomunikační operátoři chtějí společně nabídnout mobilní spojení přes satelity. Deutsche Telekom (mateřská společnost v Česku působícího T-Mobile), Orange, Telefónica a Vodafone podepsaly předběžnou dohodu o společné nabídce evropských frekvencí pro přímé spojení mobilů se satelity. Cílem je posílit evropskou technologickou nezávislost, vzniknout by mohla evropská alternativa ke Starlinku Elona Muska.</description>

<description>Česko hledá člověka, který pomůže dostat umělou inteligenci z pilotních projektů do běžného provozu napříč veřejnou správou.  <description>Rusko podle předsedkyně Evropské komise Ursuly von der Leyenové obnovuje svou vojenskou přítomnost v Arktidě, uplatňuje vůči sousedům hybridní strategie a mění bezpečnostní situaci v regionu, což má dopad na Evropskou unii.  <description>Maša Moskaljová nakreslila ve 12 letech ve škole v Jefremově, který leží asi 300 kilometrů jižně od Moskvy, protiválečný obrázek.  <description>„Rusko se vůči Ukrajině chová v pořádku. Moc toho nedělá,“ řekl americký prezident Donald Trump, když komentoval případné setkání lídrů USA, Ruska a Číny. To by se dle něj nekonalo kvůli Ukrajině. Slova pronesl ve stejný den, kdy ruský útok v Charkovské oblasti zabil šest lidí, z toho dvě děti. Předchozí noc Rusko zaútočilo na Kyjev více než tuctem balistických raket. Trump se ale k ničemu z toho nevyjádřil, uvedl server The Kyiv Independent.</description>

<description>Čtyři největ&#353;í evrop&#353;tí telekomunikační operátoři chtějí společně nabídnout mobilní spojení přes satelity. news.rawText:
Kudy z nudy – Žebříčky: Liberecký kraj Žebříčky RSS Feed <![CDATA[Dlabání dýní na Rychtě]]>

Už jste někdy nechali děti dlabat dýně v obýváku? Semínkový teror všude okolo je přesně ten důvod, proč se do toho doma raději nepouštět. Přijďte v neděli k nám! Připravili jsme správně velké dýně, které se dětem dobře dlabou, a jejich úklid zůstane na nás.

]]> Sat, 17 Oct 2026 20:31:43 GMT <![CDATA[Folkrockový večer s Filipem Šimandlem a jeho synem]]>

Chytlavé autorské příběhy ze života, poctivý folkrock a jedinečné mezigenerační propojení! Přijďte si užít vystoupení písničkáře Filipa Šimandla, kterého na klávesy doprovodí jeho čtrnáctiletý syn. Vstupné 100 Kč.

]]> Sat, 17 Oct 2026 20:18:59 GMT <![CDATA[Patrik Czuczor – Kytara napříč světem]]>

Vydejte se na hudební cestu od španělských mistrů a Latinské Ameriky až po ikonické hity Beatles nebo skupiny ABBA. Skvělý kytarový virtuóz Patrik Czuczor představí nádherné skladby i známé melodie ve vlastní úpravě. Vstupné 100 Kč.

]]> Sat, 17 Oct 2026 20:16:25 GMT <![CDATA[Mňau Mňau Band]]>

Původně vznikli jen proto, aby nemuseli na trampském festivalu žádat o pomoc kamarády. Dnes mají na kontě ocenění z Porty a míří k nám! Přijďte si užít večer plný nadsázky, akordeonu a chytlavých autorských písniček. Vstupné 100 Kč.

]]> Sat, 17 Oct 2026 20:12:53 GMT

V Jablonci funguje centrum, které vám pomůže změnit život</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903490-nezvladate-vztek-v-jablonci-funguje-centrum-ktere-vam-pomuze-zmenit-zivot.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903490-nezvladate-vztek-v-jablonci-funguje-centrum-ktere-vam-pomuze-zmenit-zivot.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 18:30:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Vztek a agresi ve vztazích se lze naučit zvládat. Regionální terapeutické centrum Stop násilí nabízí odbornou pomoc i obyvatelům Libereckého kraje, a to v Jablonci nad Nisou. Až 79 % klientů potvrzuje, že díky terapii dokázali své reakce změnit. Zjistěte, jaký udělali první krok.</description></item><item><title>Sezónní deprese není jen podzimní splín. Vyhledat pomoc včas má smysl</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zdravi/903479-sezonni-deprese-neni-jen-podzimni-splin-vyhledat-pomoc-vcas-ma-smysl.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zdravi/903479-sezonni-deprese-neni-jen-podzimni-splin-vyhledat-pomoc-vcas-ma-smysl.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 16:54:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Viktorie Beránková</dc:creator><category>Zdraví</category><description>Péče o duševní zdraví není jen otázkou podzimu. Právě kratší dny a změna denního režimu ale mohou u některých lidí zhoršit psychickou pohodu. Jak poznat běžný podzimní splín od sezónní deprese, která už zasahuje do každodenního života?</description></item><item><title>Chřipková sezóna klepe na dveře: Proč letos očkování nepodcenit?</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zdravi/903488-chripkova-sezona-klepe-na-dvere-proc-letos-ockovani-nepodcenit.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zdravi/903488-chripkova-sezona-klepe-na-dvere-proc-letos-ockovani-nepodcenit.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 15:30:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Zdraví</category><description>S příchodem podzimu opět sílí riziko respiračních infekcí a chřipky, která může mít závažné následky. Říjen a listopad představují ideální čas pro prevenci. Zjistěte, pro koho je očkování zdarma, jak se účinně chránit a na co si dát pozor při prvních příznacích.</description></item><item><title>KVÍZ: Dýně i české zvyky. Vyznáte se v podzimních tradicích?</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/kvizy/903477-kviz-dyne-i-ceske-zvyky-vyznate-se-v-podzimnich-tradicich.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/kvizy/903477-kviz-dyne-i-ceske-zvyky-vyznate-se-v-podzimnich-tradicich.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 12:12:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Nicolas Rosier</dc:creator><category>Kvízy</category><description>Vydlabané dýně, strašidelné kostýmy i vzpomínky na zesnulé blízké. Podzim se pojí s různými tradicemi, které mají překvapivě pestrou historii. Víte, odkud pochází Halloween, co se slaví v Mexiku a na kdy připadají české Dušičky? Otestujte se v našem kvízu.</description></item><item><title>V České Lípě vyjednává Živá Lípa koalici bez ANO a SPD, dohoda zatím není</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/903487-v-ceske-lipe-vyjednava-ziva-lipa-koalici-bez-ano-a-spd-dohoda-zatim-neni.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/903487-v-ceske-lipe-vyjednava-ziva-lipa-koalici-bez-ano-a-spd-dohoda-zatim-neni.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 10:31:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Politika</category><description>V České Lípě vyjednává uskupení Živá Lípa spojené se Starosty pro Liberecký kraj (SLK) koalici bez hnutí ANO, které skončilo na druhém místě. Oba subjekty mají po deseti mandátech z 25 v zastupitelstvu a v předchozích dvou volebních obdobích byly v koalici.</description></item><item><title>Galerie Lázně Liberec po čtvrt roce otevřela. Zve i na hravou výstavu Erwina Wurma</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/kultura/903470-galerie-lazne-liberec-po-ctvrt-roce-otevrela-zve-i-na-hravou-vystavu-erwina-wurma.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/kultura/903470-galerie-lazne-liberec-po-ctvrt-roce-otevrela-zve-i-na-hravou-vystavu-erwina-wurma.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 08:52:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Kultura</category><description>Po tříměsíční pauze se veřejnosti znovu otevřela Galerie Lázně v Liberci. Spolu s modernizovaným osvětlením představila hned tři nové výstavy. V jedné uvidíte absurdní a humorná díla jednoho z nejvýznamnějších světových sochařů Erwina Wurma. Ukáže jedenáctimetrový svetr či obří nakládané okurky.</description></item><item><title>Liberec letos nebude mít nové parkovací automaty, čeká na rozhodnutí ÚOHS</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/903450-liberec-letos-nebude-mit-nove-parkovaci-automaty-ceka-na-rozhodnuti-uohs.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/903450-liberec-letos-nebude-mit-nove-parkovaci-automaty-ceka-na-rozhodnuti-uohs.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 06:30:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Doprava</category><description>Liberec letos nebude mít pro městská parkoviště nové parkovací automaty, které mají nahradit zastaralé přístroje neumožňující bezhotovostní platby. Dodavatele automatů sice radnice vybrala už před dvěma měsíci, smlouvu s ním ale uzavřít nemůže. Zakázku posuzuje Úřad pro ochranu hospodářské soutěže.</description></item><item><title>Počet firemních bankrotů v Česku je nejvyšší od roku 2016</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903405-pocet-firemnich-bankrotu-v-cesku-je-nejvyssi-od-roku-2016.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903405-pocet-firemnich-bankrotu-v-cesku-je-nejvyssi-od-roku-2016.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 19 Oct 2026 20:12:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Miroslav Adamec</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>V Česku za prvních devět měsíců roku 2026 zbankrotovalo 618 obchodních společností, meziročně o 7 % více. Jde o nejvyšší počet za toto období od roku 2016. Roste také počet návrhů na bankrot, kterých soudy od ledna do září přijaly 986, což představuje meziroční zvýšení o 19 %.</description></item><item><title>Semily povedou tři nejsilnější strany, starostou bude poslanec Pražák z ANO</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/903411-semily-povedou-tri-nejsilnejsi-strany-starostou-bude-poslanec-prazak-z-ano.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/903411-semily-povedou-tri-nejsilnejsi-strany-starostou-bude-poslanec-prazak-z-ano.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 19 Oct 2026 18:30:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Politika</category><description>V Semilech vytvořilo koalici vítězné uskupení Moje Semily s ANO a Volbou pro Semily. Všechna tři uskupení získala po šesti mandátech a v zastupitelstvu tak budou mít jasnou většinu 18 z 21 hlasů. Je to racionální rozhodnutí, řekl dnes ČTK poslanec David Pražák z ANO, který by se měl stát starostou.</description></item><item><title>Regionální nemocnice nejsou zbytkem zdravotnictví, ale jeho oporou</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zdravi/903015-regionalni-nemocnice-nejsou-zbytkem-zdravotnictvi-ale-jeho-oporou.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zdravi/903015-regionalni-nemocnice-nejsou-zbytkem-zdravotnictvi-ale-jeho-oporou.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 19 Oct 2026 16:45:00 +0200</pubDate><category>Zdraví</category><description>Regionální nemocnice nelze hodnotit jen podle počtu výkonů. Drží nepřetržitou pohotovost, vzdělávají zdravotníky a přebírají pacienty k doléčení. Pokud jim centralizace vezme práci i příjmy bez náhrady, oslabí to celý systém, varuje předseda představenstva MMN Jiří Kalenský.</description></item></channel></rss>
